images.caption: Figure 1:Conceptual overview of Avatar Intelligence.(A)The maturity roadmap traces the transfer of execution and decision responsibilities from users to avatars within delegated domains.(B)A shared avatar core supports a perception–planning–decision–execution loop and task-specialized clones.(C)Evaluation accounts for both delivered value and the human effort required to obtain it: the Agentic Oversight Index,A​O​I=U−λ​PAOI=U-\lambda P, combines normalized net valueUUwith an explicit penalty for human oversight burdenPP, weighted byλ\lambda.

Figure 2:Avatar Intelligence as a user-centric operating system. A persistent user model and memory support the inner loop of perception, planning, decision, and execution. The outer ring identifies three system capabilities: work continuity, proactive service, and capability expansion. Work, assistant, social, and custom clones carry the shared user identity into distinct task contexts, connecting the avatar to tools, applications, and other agents.
Figure 4:Four application settings for Avatar Intelligence.(1)personal life,(2)organizational work,(3)financial decisions, and(4)coordination among multiple avatars.

Figure 5:Avatar Personalization through identity modeling and interaction feedback. Thought Computability and Intent Predictability connect implicit user cognition to a computable identity representation,ℐu=(zu,𝒦u)\mathcal{I}_{u}=(z_{u},\mathcal{K}_{u}), wherezuz_{u}captures personality structure and𝒦u\mathcal{K}_{u}stores user-specific knowledge and experience. Instructions, interaction traces, and environmental context inform inverse modeling of this representation, which guides actions across tasks and contexts. Feedback supports continued refinement of the user model as the user and avatar co-evolve.
